newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee widens gains, July revisits $1,700.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee widens gains, July revisits $1,700.

text.p: LIFFE robusta futures widened gains by the close on Tuesday with July rising to nearly eight-week highs on the back of funds and roaster buying.
Benchmark July rose $35 to end at $1,705 a tonne, the previous immediate resistance, after a high of $1,709. This was the highest level since March 12 when it touched $1,730.
The rise came as a belated reaction to New York's arabica futures advance on Monday, fuelled by news of a warehouse fire in Costa Rica.
"The news has blown the market up," said one trader. The London market was closed on Monday for a local holiday.
"London tried very hard to follow New York," another said. Traders noted a mixed bag of fund and roaster interest.
Traders said details on the extent of damage to the warehoused coffee remained unclear but they stressed the loss was apparently much less than the 50,000 bags originally reported.
The arabica futures headed lower on Tuesday on profit-taking to the overnight gains. The market earlier rose on news Colombian truckers threatened to launch another nationwide strike.
But profit-takers soon emerged to push prices lower.

Colombian truck drivers union officials said drivers in Cartagena port ceased operations on Monday to protest freight owners's failure to fulfill the terms of an agreement that ended a five-day strike at the end of last month.
Volume in London totalled 7,573 lots, centred on July outright and July/Sept switches. The spread stood at $12 at the close, down from $16 on Friday.
May/July switches, which stood at more than $90 late late week, narrowed to trade at around $65 on Tuesday.
Technically, the key contract still faces a hefty upside chart gap at $1,715-$1,730 before challenging $1,800.
Volume reached 3,387 lots. Traders said July/Sept switches were traded at $15-$17.
Options were fairly active, with 1,377 lots changing hands. Interest centred on September $1,450 calls and nearby July puts.

On the fundamental front, the latest International Coffee Organizsation (ICO) export data for March continued to underline the heavy front-loading of members exports following a price rally earlier this year.
Exports totalled 7.40 million 60-kg bags in March, up sharply from 6.47 in March 1996.
Other news included Nestle SA saying it might raise coffee prices by 10 to 15 percent to reflect rising market prices.

Elsewhere, German trader Berhard Rothfos said Brazil's 1997/98 coffee crop might total between 24 and 25.5 million bags compared with new estimates for 1996/97 of 30 million bags. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 5424985
